title: edgeRatio: the cevian ratio of an ordered vertex pair
content: For an n-simplex whose concurrency point has positive barycentric weights w, edgeRatio w i j is defined as w_j / w_i. For the planar triangle (n = 2) these are exactly the classical cevian division ratios BD/DC, CE/EA, AF/FB. Working with the full table of edge ratios r(i,j), rather than only the three triangle ratios, is what lets the planar Ceva equation generalize cleanly to all dimensions.

title: edgeRatio_mul: the 1-cocycle law (algebraic heart of Ceva)
content: Edge ratios chain multiplicatively: r(i,j) * r(j,k) = r(i,k). This is the single algebraic fact behind every Ceva product identity. It expresses that the edge ratios are a 1-coboundary of the weight 'potential' w on the simplex's 1-skeleton. The proof is a direct field computation once the weights are known nonzero.

title: cevaProduct3 / planar_ceva_product: classical Ceva as a 2-face product
content: Around any triangle i -> j -> k -> i of the simplex, the product of edge ratios is 1. planar_ceva_product writes this in the conventional cyclic order B -> C -> A and is precisely the classical Ceva product BD/DC * CE/EA * AF/FB = 1. The proof collapses the product by the cocycle law: r(i,j) r(j,k) r(k,i) = r(i,k) r(k,i) = r(i,i) = 1.

title: edgeRatio_cycle_prod: higher-dimensional Ceva for any closed walk
content: For edge ratios of a common point and any closed walk p(0) -> p(1) -> ... -> p(m) = p(0) through the vertices, the product of edge ratios along the walk equals 1. This is the fully general Ceva identity: the triangle case m = 3 is cevaProduct3, and the tetrahedron's 4-vertex loop is the m = 4 case. The proof rewrites each factor as w(p(t+1))/w(p(t)) and applies the telescoping lemma, so the product is w(p(m))/w(p(0)) = 1.

title: exists_weights_of_cocycle: reconstructing the concurrency point
content: The substantive converse. If a positive edge-ratio assignment r satisfies the cocycle law, then it arises from a common interior point: there exist positive barycentric weights w with r(i,j) = w_j/w_i. The weights are reconstructed explicitly as w_i = r(b,i) for any base vertex b — these are the barycentric coordinates of the concurrency point. The verification w_j/w_i = r(b,j)/r(b,i) = r(i,j) is exactly the cocycle law r(b,i) r(i,j) = r(b,j).

title: cocycle_iff_triangles: triangle conditions generate concurrency
content: For positive edge ratios, the cocycle law holds iff the classical Ceva product r(i,j) r(j,k) r(k,i) = 1 holds on every ordered triple of vertices (every triangular 2-face). The nontrivial direction starts from the cube relation r(i,i)^3 = 1, which with positivity forces r(i,i) = 1 (the factor r(i,i)^2 + r(i,i) + 1 is positive), then yields reciprocity r(i,j) r(j,i) = 1, and finally multiplicativity by cancelling the nonzero factor r(k,i).
mathContext: (\forall i j k,\ r(i,j)r(j,k) = r(i,k)) \iff (\forall i j k,\ r(i,j)r(j,k)r(k,i) = 1)

title: concurrency_iff_face_ceva: the higher-dimensional Ceva theorem
content: Combining the reconstruction with the triangle characterization: a positive edge-ratio assignment on an n-simplex comes from a common interior point if and only if the classical Ceva equation holds on every triangular face. This is the precise higher-dimensional generalization of Ceva's theorem and the answer to 'when do cevians of a simplex concur?' — they concur exactly when every 2-face satisfies the planar Ceva condition.
mathContext: (\exists\,w>0,\ r(i,j) = w_j/w_i) \iff (\forall i j k,\ r(i,j)r(j,k)r(k,i) = 1)

title: Tetrahedron (3-simplex) specializations
content: Instantiating ι = Fin 4 makes the higher-dimensional content concrete. tetrahedron_face_ceva and tetrahedron_other_face_ceva give the Ceva product = 1 on two independent triangular faces (vertices {0,1,2} and {0,1,3}), and tetrahedron_full_cycle gives product 1 around the 4-vertex closed walk 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 0. The shared reconstructed weights tie all faces to one concurrency point.
